example.target: Pregunto a una señora en la calle.
example.native: I ask a lady on the street.

example.target: Ella come en la fonda todos los días.
example.native: She eats at the small family restaurant every day.

example.target: Ella recomienda el menú del día.
example.native: She recommends the daily menu.

verbs.note: Stem change: e to ie (except nosotros).

example.target: Esperamos diez minutos en la barra.
example.native: We wait ten minutes at the counter.

example.target: Tengo hambre a las 12:30.
example.native: I am hungry at 12:30.

verbs.note: Irregular yo form (tengo) and stem change e to ie. Used in tener hambre (to be hungry).

passage.title: ¿Dónde almorzamos hoy?
target: Son las 12:30 y tengo hambre.
Pregunto a una señora en la calle: ¿Hay un buen restaurante cerca?
Ella dice que hay una fonda en la esquina.
Yo pregunto: ¿Cuánto tiempo de espera hay?
Ella responde: Casi no hay espera a esta hora.
Luego pregunto: ¿Es un lugar turístico?
Ella dice: No, es comida local y el menú del día es bueno.
Yo digo: ¿Hay mesa afuera, por favor?
Ella sonríe y contesta: Sí, hay mesas en la terraza.
native: It is 12:30 and I am hungry.
I ask a lady on the street: Is there a good restaurant nearby?
She says there is a small family restaurant on the corner.
I ask: How long is the wait?
She answers: There is almost no wait at this hour.
Then I ask: Is it a touristy place?
She says: No, it is local food and the daily menu is good.
I say: Is there a table outside, please?
She smiles and answers: Yes, there are tables on the terrace.

words.note: Common in Mexico for a simple place with home-style food.
A fixed-price lunch set; it is often called comida corrida in Mexico.
Polite form with usted, for a stranger.

example.target: El menú del día incluye postre.
example.native: The set menu includes dessert.

verbs.note: Adds y before o, e, and a endings (i to y).

example.target: Quiero el menú del día, por favor.
example.native: I want the set menu, please.

verbs.note: Stem change: e to ie, except nosotros.

example.target: Ella pide el pollo.
example.native: She orders the chicken.

verbs.note: Stem change: e to i, except nosotros.

example.target: Ella pregunta por la porción.
example.native: She asks about the portion.

example.target: ¿Tienen pescado hoy?
example.native: Do you have fish today?

verbs.note: Irregular yo form (tengo). Stem change e to ie, except nosotros.

passage.title: El menú del día
target: Una viajera entra a un restaurante a la una.
Ella pregunta: ¿Qué incluye el menú del día?
El mesero dice que incluye entrada, plato fuerte y postre.
Ella quiere saber si la bebida está incluida.
El mesero responde: Sí, incluye agua o refresco.
Ella pregunta: ¿Es una porción grande?
Él dice que la porción es mediana.
Hoy hay sopa, pollo y pescado.
Ella pide el menú del día con pollo.
native: A traveler walks into a restaurant at one o'clock.
She asks: What does the set menu include?
The waiter says it includes a starter, a main course, and dessert.
She wants to know if the drink is included.
The waiter answers: Yes, it includes water or a soft drink.
She asks: Is it a big portion?
He says the portion is medium.
Today there is soup, chicken, and fish.
She orders the set menu with chicken.

words.note: Also called plato principal.

words.en: What does the set menu include?
Can you explain the menu to me, please?
words.note: Polite request to one person, using usted.

example.target: El viajero pide tres tacos de pollo.
example.native: The traveler orders three chicken tacos.

verbs.note: Stem change: e to i.

example.target: El viajero quiere una porción pequeña.
example.native: The traveler wants a small portion.

verbs.note: Stem change: e to ie.

example.target: El vendedor pregunta: ¿Es para llevar?
example.native: The vendor asks: Is it to go?

example.target: Nosotros comemos aquí, en el puesto.
example.native: We eat here, at the stand.

passage.title: Tacos en el puesto
target: Un viajero llega a un puesto de tacos.
Hay mucha gente en el mostrador.
El viajero pregunta: ¿De qué es el taco?
El vendedor dice: Hay carne asada, pollo y al pastor.
El viajero pide tres tacos de pollo con salsa verde.
¿Es muy picante? No, es poco picante.
El viajero quiere una porción pequeña y sin cebolla.
El vendedor pregunta: ¿Es para comer aquí o para llevar?
El viajero dice: Es para llevar, por favor.
native: A traveler arrives at a taco stand.
There are many people at the counter.
The traveler asks: What is the taco filled with?
The vendor says: There is grilled beef, chicken, and al pastor.
The traveler orders three chicken tacos with green sauce.
Is it very spicy? No, it is a little spicy.
The traveler wants a small portion and no onion.
The vendor asks: Is it to eat here or to go?
The traveler says: It is to go, please.

words.note: A street-food stall.

words.en: What is the taco filled with?

words.note: Polite, with usted.

example.target: Yo quiero pan integral con pollo.
example.native: I want whole wheat bread with chicken.

verbs.note: Stem change: e to ie (not in nosotros).

example.target: ¿Puede tostar el pan?
example.native: Can you toast the bread?

verbs.note: Stem change: o to ue (not in nosotros). Use ¿Puede...? to ask politely.

example.target: ¿Puedo cambiar el queso por queso suizo?
example.native: Can I change the cheese for Swiss cheese?

example.target: El empleado pregunta qué pan quiero.
example.native: The employee asks which bread I want.

example.target: Él prepara mi sándwich.
example.native: He makes my sandwich.

passage.title: Un sándwich a mi gusto
target: Estoy en una sandwichería pequeña a la hora del almuerzo.
El empleado pregunta: ¿Qué pan quiere?
Yo quiero pan integral con pollo.
Quiero queso suizo, lechuga y tomate.
Para la mayonesa, digo: Poca mayonesa, por favor.
¿Puede tostar el pan?
El empleado dice: Sí, claro.
Luego pregunto: ¿Puedo cambiar el queso por queso suizo?
Él sonríe y prepara mi sándwich.
native: I am in a small sandwich shop at lunchtime.
The employee asks: What bread do you want?
I want whole wheat bread with chicken.
I want Swiss cheese, lettuce, and tomato.
For the mayonnaise, I say: Not much mayonnaise, please.
Can you toast the bread?
The employee says: Yes, of course.
Then I ask: Can I change the cheese for Swiss cheese?
He smiles and makes my sandwich.

words.en: I want a ham sandwich, please.
words.es: Quiero un sándwich de jamón, por favor.

words.note: Use this to ask about ingredients.

example.target: Hoy tenemos pollo con arroz y frijoles.
example.native: Today we have chicken with rice and beans.

verbs.note: Irregular: yo tengo; e to ie in most other forms.

example.target: El plato del día cuesta 9 dólares.
example.native: The daily special costs 9 dollars.

verbs.note: Stem change o to ue. You mostly use cuesta and cuestan.

example.target: El pollo lleva chile, cebolla y ajo.
example.native: The chicken has chili, onion, and garlic.

verbs.note: Also means to take something with you.

example.target: Ella pide el plato del día.
example.native: She orders the daily special.

verbs.note: Stem change e to i.

example.target: Ella le pregunta al mesero.
example.native: She asks the waiter.

passage.title: El plato del día
target: Una viajera entra a una fonda a la hora del almuerzo.
Ella le pregunta al mesero: ¿Cuál es el plato del día?
El mesero dice: Hoy tenemos pollo con arroz y frijoles.
Ella pregunta: ¿Qué lleva el pollo?
Él contesta: Lleva chile, cebolla y ajo, y es al horno.
Ella pregunta: ¿Todavía hay pollo hoy?
El mesero dice: Sí, todavía hay, y cuesta 9 dólares.
Ella dice: ¿Es rápido? Tengo poco tiempo.
Ella pide el plato del día para llevar.
native: A traveler walks into a small diner at lunchtime.
She asks the waiter: What is the daily special?
The waiter says: Today we have chicken with rice and beans.
She asks: What is in the chicken?
He answers: It has chili, onion, and garlic, and it is baked.
She asks: Is there still chicken today?
The waiter says: Yes, there is still some, and it costs 9 dollars.
She says: Is it fast? I have little time.
She orders the daily special to go.

words.note: Also called comida corrida in Mexico, a set lunch.
Use mesera for a woman.
Literally: what does it carry. Very common for ingredients.

words.en: Is it a good choice for a quick lunch?
words.es: ¿Es una buena opción para un almuerzo rápido?

words.note: Polite, uses usted.

example.target: Luego pide la sopa de tortilla.
example.native: Then he orders the tortilla soup.

verbs.note: Stem change: e to i.

example.target: El viajero pregunta: ¿La porción es grande o chica?
example.native: The traveler asks: Is the portion big or small?

example.target: ¿Qué me recomienda, la sopa o el arroz?
example.native: What do you recommend, the soup or the rice?

verbs.note: Stem change: e to ie.

example.target: Voy a probar el arroz de mi amigo.
example.native: I am going to try my friend's rice.

verbs.note: Stem change: o to ue.

example.target: Prefiero la salsa suave.
example.native: I prefer a mild sauce.

verbs.note: Stem change: e to ie.

passage.title: Elegir entre sopa y arroz
target: Un viajero entra a una fonda pequeña a la hora de la comida.
Primero le pregunta al mesero: ¿Qué me recomienda, la sopa de tortilla o el arroz con pollo?
El mesero explica que la sopa es tradicional de la región y que viene con aguacate.
Después el viajero pregunta: ¿La porción es grande o chica?
El mesero dice que el arroz es una porción grande y que la salsa lleva chile.
El viajero pregunta: ¿Es muy picante? Prefiero la salsa suave.
Luego pide la sopa de tortilla y va a probar el arroz de su amigo.
Al final dice: Voy a pedir la sopa, y también quisiera un vaso de agua, por favor.
native: A traveler walks into a small eatery at lunchtime.
First he asks the waiter: What do you recommend, the tortilla soup or the rice with chicken?
The waiter explains that the soup is traditional in the region and comes with avocado.
Then the traveler asks: Is the portion big or small?
The waiter says the rice is a big portion and the sauce has chili.
The traveler asks: Is it very spicy? I prefer a mild sauce.
Then he orders the tortilla soup and is going to try his friend's rice.
In the end he says: I'm going to order the soup, and I would also like a glass of water, please.

words.note: Common in Mexico and the US. Use mesera for a woman.
Polite form with usted.

words.en: Is the portion big or small?
Is it a traditional dish of the region?
words.es: ¿Es un plato tradicional de la región?

words.en: What is the difference between the two?
words.es: ¿Cuál es la diferencia entre los dos?

words.en: I would like the soup, please.

example.target: Nosotros compartimos la ensalada y las papas fritas.
example.native: We share the salad and the french fries.

example.target: Pedimos una pizza para la mesa.
example.native: We order a pizza for the table.

verbs.note: Stem change: e to i (pido, pides, pide, piden).

example.target: Dividimos la pizza en partes iguales.
example.native: We divide the pizza into equal parts.

example.target: El mesero trae cuatro platos.
example.native: The waiter brings four plates.

verbs.note: Irregular yo form: traigo.

example.target: Yo pregunto si es normal compartir.
example.native: I ask if it is normal to share.

verbs.note: Use preguntar for questions and pedir for requests.

passage.title: Compartir platos en la mesa
target: Somos cuatro amigos en un restaurante y queremos probar varios platos.
Primero le pregunto al mesero: ¿Es normal compartir los platos aquí?
Él sonríe y dice: Sí, muchos clientes piden platos para compartir.
Entonces pedimos una pizza, una ensalada y unas papas fritas para la mesa.
Después le digo: ¿Nos puede traer platos extra y cubiertos, por favor?
El mesero nos trae cuatro platos y una cuchara grande para servir.
Ahora vamos a dividir la pizza en partes iguales.
Al final, pedimos la cuenta y le preguntamos si podemos pagar por separado.
native: We are four friends in a restaurant and we want to try several dishes.
First I ask the waiter: Is it normal to share dishes here?
He smiles and says: Yes, many customers order dishes to share.
Then we order a pizza, a salad, and some french fries for the table.
Afterward I say to him: Can you bring us extra plates and silverware, please?
The waiter brings us four plates and a big spoon for serving.
Now we are going to divide the pizza into equal parts.
In the end, we ask for the check and we ask him if we can pay separately.

words.note: Means both the plate and the dish of food.
Usually plural.
Common in Mexico and the US; use mesera for a woman.

words.en: Is it normal to share dishes here?
Can you bring us extra plates, please?
words.es: ¿Nos puede traer platos extra, por favor?
words.note: Polite form with usted.

words.en: We want to share everything in the middle of the table.
words.es: Queremos compartir todo en el centro de la mesa.

words.en: Can you divide the pizza into four?
How many portions does this dish come with?

example.target: Le pregunto al mesero por los ingredientes.
example.native: I ask the waiter about the ingredients.

example.target: Pido la ensalada sin carne.
example.native: I order the salad without meat.

verbs.note: Stem change: e to i.

verbs.native: to contain, to have in it

example.target: ¿Los frijoles llevan manteca?
example.native: Do the beans have lard?

verbs.note: Llevar also means to carry or to take. For food, it means what is in the dish.

example.target: ¿Puede quitar el queso, por favor?
example.native: Can you remove the cheese, please?

verbs.note: Stem change: o to ue.

example.target: Ellos quitan la carne del plato si es posible.
example.native: They take the meat out of the dish if it is possible.

passage.title: Pregunto por los ingredientes
target: Es mediodía y entro a una fonda pequeña para almorzar.
Primero, leo el plato del día en la pizarra.
Después le pregunto al mesero: ¿Qué ingredientes tiene este plato?
Le explico: Soy vegetariano, ¿hay algo sin carne?
Luego pregunto: ¿Los frijoles llevan manteca o caldo de pollo?
El mesero va a preguntar en la cocina y regresa con la respuesta.
Según la cocina, la ensalada lleva queso, pero no lleva carne.
Yo digo: Entiendo que no pueden garantizar nada, pero gracias por revisar.
Voy a pedir la ensalada sin carne y con la salsa aparte.
native: It is noon and I walk into a small family restaurant to have lunch.
First, I read the daily special on the board.
Then I ask the waiter: What ingredients does this dish have?
I explain to him: I am vegetarian, is there something without meat?
Next I ask: Do the beans have lard or chicken broth?
The waiter is going to ask in the kitchen and comes back with the answer.
According to the kitchen, the salad has cheese, but it has no meat.
I say: I understand you cannot guarantee anything, but thank you for checking.
I am going to order the salad without meat and with the sauce on the side.

words.note: Also called comida corrida in many Mexican restaurants.
Use mesera for a woman.
Often hidden in soups, rice, and beans.
Common in beans and tortillas in Mexican cooking.
Use only for a real allergy; for a preference say evito or no como.

words.en: What ingredients does this dish have?
I am vegetarian, is there something without meat?
words.note: A woman says vegetariana.

words.en: Do the beans have lard or chicken broth?
words.es: ¿Los frijoles llevan manteca o caldo de pollo?

words.en: Can you remove the cheese, please?
words.note: Use usted with a waiter.

words.en: I understand you cannot guarantee anything.
words.es: Entiendo que no pueden garantizar nada.
words.note: Polite way to show you are not demanding a guarantee.

words.en: Can you ask in the kitchen, please?
words.es: ¿Puede preguntar en la cocina, por favor?

example.target: Yo pido pan y mantequilla.
example.native: I ask for bread and butter.

verbs.note: Stem change: e to i.

example.target: El mesero trae el menú.
example.native: The waiter brings the menu.

verbs.note: Irregular yo form: traigo.

example.target: La botella cuesta extra.
example.native: The bottle costs extra.

verbs.note: Stem change: o to ue. Mostly used in the third person.

example.target: ¿Cobran por el pan?
example.native: Do you charge for the bread?

verbs.note: Se cobra means it is charged.

example.target: El viajero pregunta si el agua es gratis.
example.native: The traveler asks if the water is free.

verbs.note: Use preguntar for questions and pedir for requests.

passage.title: Agua y pan en la mesa
target: Primero, un viajero llega a una trattoria y se sienta en una mesa pequeña.
El mesero trae el menú y pregunta: ¿Qué va a tomar?
El viajero dice: ¿Me puede traer agua, por favor?
Después pregunta: ¿El agua es gratis o se cobra?
El mesero explica que el agua de la jarra es gratis, pero la botella cuesta extra.
Entonces el viajero pide pan y mantequilla, y pregunta si el pan tiene cargo.
El mesero dice que el pan es cortesía de la casa.
Luego el viajero pide sal, servilletas y salsa picante para la mesa.
Al final, va a pedir la cuenta y revisar que todo esté bien.
native: First, a traveler arrives at a trattoria and sits at a small table.
The waiter brings the menu and asks: What are you going to drink?
The traveler says: Can you bring me water, please?
Then he asks: Is the water free, or is there a charge?
The waiter explains that the pitcher water is free, but the bottle costs extra.
Then the traveler asks for bread and butter, and asks whether the bread has a charge.
The waiter says the bread is complimentary from the house.
Next the traveler asks for salt, napkins, and hot sauce for the table.
In the end, he is going to ask for the bill and check that everything is right.

words.note: Takes el in the singular: el agua.

words.en: Can you bring me water, please?
words.note: Polite request with usted.

words.en: Is there any charge for the bread?
Is the water free, or is there a charge?
words.es: ¿El agua es gratis o se cobra?

words.en: I would like pitcher water, please.
words.es: Quiero agua de la jarra, por favor.

words.en: Could you bring me more napkins, please?

example.target: Ana pide la cuenta.
example.native: Ana asks for the check.

verbs.note: Stem change: e to i (pido, pides, pide, piden).

example.target: El mesero trae la sopa rápido.
example.native: The waiter brings the soup quickly.

verbs.note: Irregular yo form: traigo.

example.target: Ana decide pedir el sándwich.
example.native: Ana decides to order the sandwich.

example.target: El plato del día tarda 15 minutos.
example.native: The daily special takes 15 minutes.

verbs.note: Used to ask how long something takes: ¿Cuánto tarda?

example.target: Ana come rápido porque tiene poco tiempo.
example.native: Ana eats quickly because she has little time.

verbs.note: In Mexico, comer can also mean to have the main midday meal.

passage.title: Un almuerzo rápido
target: Ana entra a un restaurante cerca del museo y busca una mesa.
Primero le dice al mesero: Solo tengo 20 minutos para comer.
Luego pregunta: ¿Qué platillo puede llegar rápido?
El mesero dice que el plato del día tarda 15 minutos, pero la sopa y el sándwich salen más rápido.
Ana decide: Voy a pedir el sándwich, por favor.
También quiere una ensalada pequeña y una bebida fría.
Después pide: ¿Me puede traer la cuenta ahora?
Así termina su almuerzo y llega al museo a tiempo.
native: Ana walks into a restaurant near the museum and looks for a table.
First she tells the waiter: I only have 20 minutes to eat.
Then she asks: Which dish can arrive quickly?
The waiter says the daily special takes 15 minutes, but the soup and the sandwich come out faster.
Ana decides: I'm going to order the sandwich, please.
She also wants a small salad and a cold drink.
Afterward she asks: Can you bring me the check now?
This way she finishes her lunch and gets to the museum on time.

words.note: Use mesera for a woman. Both are common in Mexico and the US.

words.en: I only have 20 minutes to eat.

words.note: Platillo is a common word for a dish on a menu in Mexico.

words.en: How long does the daily special take?
I'm going to order the sandwich, please.
words.es: Voy a pedir el sándwich, por favor.

words.en: Can you bring me the check now?
words.note: Polite form with usted.

words.en: Do you have something that comes out fast?

example.target: Esperamos el pedido desde hace mucho tiempo.
example.native: We have been waiting for the order for a long time.

verbs.note: Esperar also means to hope.

example.target: El mesero revisa el pedido en la cocina.
example.native: The waiter checks the order in the kitchen.

example.target: El mesero trae otro refresco.
example.native: The waiter brings another soft drink.

verbs.note: Irregular yo form: traigo.

example.target: Si la sopa está fría, pido otra.
example.native: If the soup is cold, I ask for another one.

verbs.note: Stem change: e to i (pido, pides, pide, piden).

example.target: El mesero quita el plato de la cuenta.
example.native: The waiter takes the dish off the bill.

passage.title: Mi plato nunca llegó
target: Estoy en una fonda con mis amigos, y ellos ya terminaron el plato del día.
Mi pedido todavía no llega, y llevamos 40 minutos esperando.
Llamo al mesero con calma y le digo: ¿Puede revisar mi pedido, por favor?
El mesero va a la cocina y dice que hay un problema con la sopa.
Le explico que no quiero comida fría porque mis amigos ya terminaron.
Además, nos falta un refresco para la mesa.
Pregunto: ¿Podemos quitar este plato de la cuenta?
El mesero ofrece quitar el plato y traer otro refresco.
Le doy las gracias porque la solución es justa y todos quedamos contentos.
native: I am at a small diner with my friends, and they already finished the daily special.
My order still has not arrived, and we have been waiting 40 minutes.
I call the waiter calmly and say to him: Can you check my order, please?
The waiter goes to the kitchen and says there is a problem with the soup.
I explain that I do not want cold food because my friends already finished.
Also, we are missing a soft drink for the table.
I ask: Can we take this dish off the bill?
The waiter offers to remove the dish and bring another soft drink.
I thank him because the solution is fair and everyone is happy.

words.note: Use mesera for a woman.
In Mexico and the US, you ask for la cuenta to pay.

words.en: Excuse me, my soup is cold.
words.note: Disculpe is polite when you speak to one server.

words.en: Excuse me, we are missing a soft drink.
Can you check my order, please?
Can we take this dish off the bill?
words.es: ¿Podemos quitar este plato de la cuenta?

words.en: What solution can you offer us?

example.target: Al final pago en efectivo.
example.native: In the end I pay in cash.

verbs.note: Use pagar con tarjeta and pagar en efectivo.

example.target: Dividimos la cuenta por persona.
example.native: We split the bill by person.

verbs.note: Dividir la cuenta is the usual way to say split the bill.

example.target: Mi amiga pide solo su platillo y su bebida.
example.native: My friend orders only her dish and her drink.

verbs.note: Stem change: e to i.

example.target: El mesero cobra cada tarjeta por separado.
example.native: The waiter charges each card separately.

example.target: Cada uno deja la propina que quiere.
example.native: Each person leaves the tip they want.

verbs.note: Dejar propina means to leave a tip.

passage.title: Dividir la cuenta del almuerzo
target: Somos cuatro viajeros y acabamos de comer en un restaurante pequeño.
Le digo al mesero: ¿Me puede traer la cuenta, por favor?
Cuando llega, le pregunto: ¿Podemos dividir la cuenta por persona?
Él dice que sí, pero necesita saber cómo vamos a pagar.
Yo explico: Vamos a hacer dos pagos con tarjeta y uno en efectivo.
Mi amiga pide solo su platillo y su bebida, porque los demás compartimos los postres.
Antes de pagar, pregunto: ¿La propina ya está incluida en el total?
El mesero dice que no, así que cada uno deja la cantidad que quiere.
Al final pago en efectivo, recibo el cambio y guardo el recibo.
native: We are four travelers and we have just eaten at a small restaurant.
I say to the waiter: Can you bring me the bill, please?
When he arrives, I ask him: Can we split the bill by person?
He says yes, but he needs to know how we are going to pay.
I explain: We are going to make two card payments and one cash payment.
My friend orders only her dish and her drink, because the rest of us share the desserts.
Before paying, I ask: Is the tip already included in the total?
The waiter says it is not, so each person leaves the amount they want.
In the end I pay in cash, receive the change, and keep the receipt.

words.note: Use mesera for a woman. In Mexico and the US, mesero is the usual word.
Common in Mexico for a menu dish.
Ask whether it is already included before you pay.

words.en: Can you bring me the bill, please?
words.es: ¿Me puede traer la cuenta, por favor?
words.note: Polite, formal form with usted.

words.en: Can we split the bill by person?
Can you charge us for each dish separately?
words.es: ¿Nos puede cobrar cada platillo por separado?
words.note: Use this to split by item.

words.en: We are going to make two card payments and one cash payment.
words.es: Vamos a hacer dos pagos con tarjeta y uno en efectivo.

words.en: Is the tip already included in the total?
words.es: ¿La propina ya está incluida en el total?

words.en: Do you accept card, or only cash?

example.target: Felicito al chef por el plato del día.
example.native: I congratulate the chef for the daily special.

example.target: Esta salsa me recuerda la cocina de mi abuela.
example.native: This sauce reminds me of my grandmother's cooking.

verbs.note: Stem change o to ue. To say it reminds me, use me recuerda.

example.target: Le agradezco mucho la atención.
example.native: I thank you very much for the service.

verbs.note: Irregular yo form: agradezco.

example.target: Recomiendo este plato a todos mis amigos.
example.native: I recommend this dish to all my friends.

verbs.note: Stem change e to ie.

example.target: Le digo al mesero que todo estuvo delicioso.
example.native: I tell the waiter that everything was delicious.

verbs.note: Stem change e to i, and yo is irregular: digo.

passage.title: Gracias al chef
target: Al terminar el almuerzo en la trattoria, llamo al mesero y le digo: ¡Todo estuvo delicioso!
Quiero felicitar al chef, porque el plato del día fue extraordinario.
La salsa tenía un sabor casero y los ingredientes eran muy frescos.
Me recordó la cocina de mi abuela, y por eso casi me emociono.
¿Podría decirle al chef que le doy las gracias de parte mía?
El mesero sonríe y me pregunta si quiero hablar con él en persona.
Si tiene un minuto, me encantaría saludarlo, pero si está ocupado, entiendo.
Antes de salir, pido la cuenta y dejo una buena propina para todo el equipo.
native: After finishing lunch at the trattoria, I call the waiter and tell him: Everything was delicious!
I want to congratulate the chef, because the daily special was extraordinary.
The sauce had a homemade flavor and the ingredients were very fresh.
It reminded me of my grandmother's cooking, and that is why I almost get emotional.
Could you tell the chef that I send my thanks?
The waiter smiles and asks me if I want to talk with him in person.
If he has a minute, I would love to say hello, but if he is busy, I understand.
Before leaving, I ask for the bill and leave a good tip for the whole team.

words.note: Also said: cocinero or cocinera.
Mesera for a woman. Common in Mexico and the US.

words.en: Could you tell the chef thank you very much?
words.es: ¿Podría decirle al chef que muchas gracias?
words.note: Polite request using podría.

words.en: I want to congratulate the chef for this dish.
words.es: Quiero felicitar al chef por este plato.

words.en: It reminded me of my grandmother's cooking.
words.es: Me recordó la cocina de mi abuela.

words.en: What is in the sauce? It is incredible.
Could I say hello to the chef, if he has time?
words.es: ¿Podría saludar al chef, si tiene tiempo?

example.target: Mañana almorzamos cerca del mercado.
example.native: Tomorrow we have lunch near the market.

verbs.note: Stem change: o to ue (except nosotros).

example.target: Te invito a almorzar mañana.
example.native: I invite you to have lunch tomorrow.

verbs.note: Invitar often implies you will pay, so say each one pays if you mean to split.

example.target: ¿Prefieres comer adentro o afuera?
example.native: Do you prefer to eat inside or outside?

verbs.note: Stem change: e to ie (except nosotros).

example.target: Si no puedes mañana, podemos ir otro día.
example.native: If you can't tomorrow, we can go another day.

verbs.note: Stem change: o to ue (except nosotros).

verbs.native: to meet up, to suit (a time)

example.target: ¿Quedamos a la 1:00 en la entrada?
example.native: Shall we meet at 1:00 at the entrance?

verbs.note: The we form is a common way to fix a meeting time with someone.

passage.title: Una invitación a almorzar
target: Estoy de viaje y hablo con Marta, una conocida de mi hotel.
Le digo: ¿Te gustaría almorzar conmigo mañana, si no tienes otro plan?
Ella contesta que sí, porque tiene hambre y conoce una fonda cerca del mercado.
Yo pregunto: ¿A qué hora te queda bien?
Marta propone la 1:00 de la tarde, porque antes tiene que trabajar.
Me parece perfecto, y le pregunto si prefiere ir a otro lugar con mesa afuera.
Ella dice que la fonda tiene menú del día y que es un lugar tranquilo.
Si no puede ir, no hay problema, y yo acepto su respuesta con una sonrisa.
Al final, decidimos vernos en la entrada del mercado y cada quien paga lo suyo.
native: I am traveling and I talk with Marta, an acquaintance from my hotel.
I say to her: Would you like to have lunch with me tomorrow, if you have no other plan?
She answers yes, because she is hungry and knows a small family restaurant near the market.
I ask: What time works for you?
Marta suggests 1:00 in the afternoon, because she has to work before then.
It sounds perfect to me, and I ask her if she prefers to go to another place with an outdoor table.
She says the restaurant has a daily special and that it is a quiet place.
If she can't go, there is no problem, and I accept her answer with a smile.
In the end, we decide to meet at the market entrance and each person pays for their own.

words.note: Common in Mexico for a simple, homestyle eatery.

words.en: Would you like to have lunch with me tomorrow?
words.note: Soft and low-pressure. Use Le gustaría with someone you address as usted.

words.es: Si no puedes, no hay problema.

words.en: Sure, that sounds perfect to me.
Another day, then. Thanks for telling me.
words.es: Otro día será, gracias por decirme.

example.target: Al final, pido la cuenta.
example.native: At the end, I ask for the bill.

verbs.note: Stem change e to i (pido, pides, pide, piden); nosotros stays pedimos.

example.target: ¿Podemos pagar por separado?
example.native: Can we pay separately?

verbs.native: to contain, to have in it (a dish)

example.target: ¿Este plato lleva nueces?
example.native: Does this dish have nuts?

verbs.note: Llevar also means to carry or to take; with food it means what the dish contains.

example.target: Elena y yo buscamos un lugar con menú del día.
example.native: Elena and I look for a place with a set lunch menu.

verbs.note: No preposition after it: buscar un lugar means to look for a place.

example.target: Tengo alergia a las nueces.
example.native: I'm allergic to nuts.

verbs.note: Irregular yo form (tengo) and stem change e to ie (tienes, tiene, tienen).

passage.title: Un almuerzo con Elena
target: Primero, Elena y yo buscamos un lugar con menú del día cerca del museo.
En la puerta le pregunto al mesero: ¿Tiene una mesa para dos?
Después leemos el menú y Elena dice: Vamos a pedir el menú del día.
Tengo alergia a las nueces, así que pregunto: ¿Este plato lleva nueces?
El mesero revisa los ingredientes con la cocina y dice: No, no lleva nueces.
Luego llega una ensalada, y le digo: Disculpe, yo pedí la sopa, no la ensalada.
Al final, pido la cuenta y pregunto: ¿Podemos pagar por separado?
El mesero dice que sí, y dejamos una propina en la mesa.
native: First, Elena and I look for a place with a set lunch menu near the museum.
At the door I ask the server: Do you have a table for two?
Then we read the menu and Elena says: We're going to order the set lunch menu.
I'm allergic to nuts, so I ask: Does this dish have nuts?
The server checks the ingredients with the kitchen and says: No, it doesn't have nuts.
Next a salad arrives, and I tell him: Excuse me, I ordered the soup, not the salad.
At the end, I ask for the bill and ask: Can we pay separately?
The server says yes, and we leave a tip on the table.

words.note: In Mexico you will also hear comida corrida for a fixed-price lunch.
Mesero/mesera is used in Mexico and Latin America; in Spain people say camarero.
Say tengo alergia a... (I'm allergic to...).
Tipping customs vary by country; ask locally or check the bill to see if service is included.

words.en: Do you have a table for two?
words.note: Tiene is the polite usted form, right for talking to a server.

words.en: We're going to order the set lunch menu.
words.es: Vamos a pedir el menú del día.

words.note: Llevar is the usual verb for what a dish contains.

words.en: Excuse me, I ordered the soup, not the salad.
words.es: Disculpe, yo pedí la sopa, no la ensalada.

example.target: Primero tomo una charola y cubiertos.
example.native: First I take a tray and cutlery.

example.target: Pido la sopa de primer tiempo.
example.native: I order the soup for the first course.

verbs.note: Stem change e to i (except nosotros).

example.target: De segundo tiempo, escojo el guisado de pollo.
example.native: For the second course, I choose the chicken stew.

verbs.note: Spelling change in the yo form: g becomes j (escojo).

example.target: Pago en la caja antes de sentarme.
example.native: I pay at the register before sitting down.

example.target: Me siento en una mesa libre.
example.native: I sit down at a free table.

verbs.note: Stem change e to ie (except nosotros). Reflexive: keep the pronoun.

passage.title: Almuerzo en el comedor
target: A mediodía, entro a un comedor de trabajadores cerca del mercado.
Primero tomo una charola y cubiertos, y luego le pregunto a un señor: ¿Dónde empieza la fila?
El letrero dice que el menú del día cuesta 95 pesos e incluye agua fresca.
La cocinera me pregunta: ¿Qué va a querer de primer tiempo?
Le digo: De primer tiempo, quiero la sopa, por favor, y de segundo tiempo, el guisado de pollo.
Después pregunto: ¿Se paga primero en la caja?
Ella dice que sí, así que pago en la caja antes de sentarme.
Al final no veo ninguna mesa libre, así que le pregunto a una trabajadora: ¿Está libre este lugar?
native: At midday, I walk into a workers' canteen near the market.
First I take a tray and cutlery, and then I ask a man: Where does the line start?
The sign says the daily set menu costs 95 pesos and includes agua fresca.
The cook asks me: What are you going to have for the first course?
I tell her: For the first course, I want the soup, please, and for the second course, the chicken stew.
Then I ask: Do you pay first at the register?
She says yes, so I pay at the register before sitting down.
In the end I don't see any free table, so I ask a worker: Is this seat free?

words.note: Also means dining room; a comedor de trabajadores or comedor económico serves cheap set lunches.
Common in Mexico; you will also hear bandeja elsewhere.
In Mexico courses are often called tiempos; primer plato is also understood.
A light drink made from water, fruit and sugar, often included with the set lunch.

words.en: What comes with the daily set menu?
For the first course, I want the soup, please.
words.es: De primer tiempo, quiero la sopa, por favor.

words.en: Do you pay first at the register?

example.target: ¿Nos puede traer un plato extra?
example.native: Can you bring us an extra plate?

verbs.note: Irregular yo form: traigo.

example.target: La cocina prepara una porción pequeña.
example.native: The kitchen prepares a small portion.

example.target: Mi bebé y yo compartimos mi plato.
example.native: My baby and I share my plate.

example.target: Mi hijo solo come pasta sola.
example.native: My son only eats plain pasta.

passage.title: Almuerzo con los niños
target: Ana llega a una trattoria a la hora del almuerzo con su hijo de 6 años y su bebé.
Primero, le pregunta al mesero: ¿Tienen una silla alta para la bebé?
Luego mira el menú y pregunta: ¿Tienen porciones para niños?
El mesero contesta: No tenemos menú infantil, pero la cocina puede preparar una porción pequeña.
Ana explica: Mi hijo solo come pasta sola, sin salsa, con un poco de mantequilla.
Después pregunta: ¿Cuánto cuesta la porción pequeña?
El mesero dice: Según el gerente, cuesta 6 euros, la mitad del plato normal.
Al final, Ana decide: Mi bebé va a comer de mi plato, ¿nos puede traer un plato extra para compartir?
native: Ana arrives at a trattoria at lunchtime with her 6-year-old son and her baby.
First, she asks the waiter: Do you have a high chair for the baby?
Then she looks at the menu and asks: Do you have children's portions?
The waiter answers: We don't have a kids' menu, but the kitchen can prepare a small portion.
Ana explains: My son only eats plain pasta, without sauce, with a little butter.
After that she asks: How much does the small portion cost?
The waiter says: According to the manager, it costs 6 euros, half of the regular dish.
In the end, Ana decides: My baby is going to eat from my plate, can you bring us an extra plate to share?

words.note: In Mexico you will also hear silla periquera.
Sola here means with nothing added.
Mexican usage; in Spain you will hear camarero.

words.en: Do you have a high chair for the baby?
words.es: ¿Tienen una silla alta para la bebé?
words.note: Use para el bebé for a baby boy.

words.en: Can the kitchen prepare plain pasta, without sauce?
words.es: ¿La cocina puede preparar pasta sola, sin salsa?

words.en: How much does the small portion cost?
Can you bring us an extra plate to share?
words.es: ¿Nos puede traer un plato extra para compartir?
words.note: Puede (usted) is the polite form for a waiter.

example.target: Ana llama a la Trattoria Rosa antes del almuerzo.
example.native: Ana calls Trattoria Rosa before lunch.

example.target: ¿Tienen entrada sin escalones?
example.native: Do you have step-free entry?

verbs.note: Irregular: the yo form is tengo, and the stem changes e to ie (tienes, tiene, tienen).

example.target: ¿Me puede decir dónde está la rampa?
example.native: Can you tell me where the ramp is?

verbs.note: Stem change o to ue in every form except nosotros.

example.target: Mi mamá usa andadera.
example.native: My mom uses a walker.

example.target: Necesitamos espacio para una silla de ruedas.
example.native: We need space for a wheelchair.

passage.title: Una llamada antes del almuerzo
target: Ana llama a la Trattoria Rosa antes del almuerzo.
Primero pregunta: ¿Tienen entrada sin escalones?
El mesero contesta: Sí, hay una rampa al lado de la puerta principal.
Después Ana pregunta: ¿El baño es accesible para silla de ruedas?
El mesero dice: Sí, y el pasillo es ancho.
Luego Ana explica: Mi papá usa silla de ruedas y mi mamá usa andadera.
Ana pregunta: ¿Hay espacio para una silla de ruedas en la mesa?
El mesero responde: Sí, vamos a preparar una mesa tranquila cerca de la ventana.
Ana dice: Perfecto, quiero hacer una reservación para 4 personas a la 1:00.
native: Ana calls Trattoria Rosa before lunch.
First she asks: Do you have step-free entry?
The waiter answers: Yes, there is a ramp next to the main door.
Then Ana asks: Is the restroom wheelchair accessible?
The waiter says: Yes, and the hallway is wide.
Next Ana explains: My dad uses a wheelchair and my mom uses a walker.
Ana asks: Is there space for a wheelchair at the table?
The waiter replies: Yes, we are going to set up a quiet table near the window.
Ana says: Perfect, I want to make a reservation for 4 people at 1:00.

words.note: In Mexico and the US, people say baño for a public restroom. Sanitario shows up on signs.
Andadera is the common Mexican word. In other countries you may hear andador.
Reservación is common in Mexico and the US. In Spain people say reserva.

words.es: ¿El baño es accesible para silla de ruedas?

words.en: Is there space for a wheelchair at the table?
words.es: ¿Hay espacio para una silla de ruedas en la mesa?

words.en: Is there a quiet table available?
Can you tell me where the ramp is?
words.es: ¿Me puede decir dónde está la rampa?
words.note: Use puede (usted) when you talk to staff. It is polite.

words.es: Mi papá usa silla de ruedas.

example.target: Mi pareja tiene una alergia grave a los mariscos.
example.native: My partner has a severe allergy to shellfish.

verbs.note: Irregular yo form (tengo) and e to ie stem change.

example.target: ¿Usan la misma freidora para los camarones?
example.native: Do you use the same fryer for the shrimp?

verbs.native: to contain, to have in it (food)

example.target: El caldo de la sopa del día lleva mariscos.
example.native: The stock for the soup of the day has shellfish in it.

verbs.note: Usually means to carry; with food it means what a dish contains.

example.target: ¿Puede preguntar en la cocina, por favor?
example.native: Can you ask in the kitchen, please?

example.target: Gracias, pero vamos a comer en otro lugar.
example.native: Thank you, but we are going to eat somewhere else.

passage.title: Una alergia grave en la fonda
target: Ana y su pareja Tom entran a una fonda pequeña para el almuerzo.
Primero, Ana le dice al mesero: Mi pareja tiene una alergia grave a los mariscos.
Luego explica: Incluso una cantidad pequeña le causa una reacción grave.
Después pregunta: ¿Usan la misma freidora para los camarones?
El mesero contesta: Sí, es la misma freidora, y el caldo de la sopa del día lleva mariscos.
Ana pregunta: ¿Puede preguntar en la cocina, por favor?
El mesero regresa y dice: El cocinero dice que la salsa también lleva camarón seco.
Ana ve el riesgo de contaminación cruzada y dice: Gracias, pero vamos a comer en otro lugar.
native: Ana and her partner Tom go into a small diner for lunch.
First, Ana tells the waiter: My partner has a severe allergy to shellfish.
Then she explains: Even a small amount causes him a severe reaction.
After that she asks: Do you use the same fryer for the shrimp?
The waiter answers: Yes, it is the same fryer, and the stock for the soup of the day has shellfish in it.
Ana asks: Can you ask in the kitchen, please?
The waiter comes back and says: The cook says that the sauce also has dried shrimp in it.
Ana sees the risk of cross-contamination and says: Thank you, but we are going to eat somewhere else.

words.note: Mariscos covers shrimp, crab, clams and similar seafood; fish is pescado.
In Spain you may hear gambas instead.
Mexican usage; in Spain it is camarero.

words.en: My partner has a severe allergy to shellfish.
words.es: Mi pareja tiene una alergia grave a los mariscos.

words.en: Do you use the same fryer for the shrimp?
words.es: ¿Usan la misma freidora para los camarones?

words.en: Does the stock have shellfish in it?
words.note: Llevar is the everyday way to ask what is in a dish.

words.en: Can you ask in the kitchen, please?
words.es: ¿Puede preguntar en la cocina, por favor?

words.en: What ingredients does the sauce have?
Thank you, but we are going to eat somewhere else.
words.es: Gracias, pero vamos a comer en otro lugar.

example.target: Después del almuerzo, Ana pide la cuenta.
example.native: After lunch, Ana asks for the bill.

verbs.note: Stem change e to i (pido, pides), except nosotros: pedimos.

example.target: Primero Ana revisa el total.
example.native: First Ana checks the total.

example.target: Disculpe, ¿me puede explicar este cargo?
example.native: Excuse me, can you explain this charge to me?

example.target: El mesero quita el pan de la cuenta.
example.native: The waiter removes the bread from the bill.

example.target: Ana paga el nuevo total con tarjeta.
example.native: Ana pays the new total by card.

verbs.note: Pagar takes no preposition: pagar la cuenta means to pay the bill.

passage.title: Un cargo inesperado
target: Después del almuerzo, Ana pide la cuenta en una pequeña trattoria.
Primero revisa el total y ve un cargo por el pan, otro por el cubierto y un cargo por servicio del 10%.
Luego llama al mesero y le dice: Disculpe, ¿me puede explicar este cargo?
Ana explica con calma: No pedí el pan, y el cargo por servicio no está en el menú.
El mesero revisa la cuenta y dice: Tiene razón, voy a quitar el pan.
También explica: El cubierto es de 2 euros por persona, según la política del restaurante.
Ana responde: Está bien, pago el cubierto, pero no el cargo por servicio.
Al final, el mesero corrige la cuenta y Ana paga el nuevo total con tarjeta.
native: After lunch, Ana asks for the bill at a small trattoria.
First she checks the total and sees a charge for the bread, another for the cover, and a 10% service charge.
Then she calls the waiter and says: Excuse me, can you explain this charge to me?
Ana explains calmly: I didn't order the bread, and the service charge isn't on the menu.
The waiter checks the bill and says: You're right, I'm going to remove the bread.
He also explains: The cover is 2 euros per person, according to the restaurant's policy.
Ana answers: That's fine, I'll pay the cover, but not the service charge.
In the end, the waiter corrects the bill and Ana pays the new total by card.

words.note: In restaurants, ask for la cuenta, not la factura (an invoice).
Mostly used in Spain, Italy-style restaurants and Argentina; it also means place setting.
Mesero in Mexico and much of Latin America; camarero in Spain.

words.en: Excuse me, can you explain this charge to me?
words.note: Using usted and disculpe keeps the question calm and polite.

words.en: The service charge isn't on the menu.
words.es: El cargo por servicio no está en el menú.

words.en: Can you correct the bill, please?
words.es: ¿Me puede corregir la cuenta, por favor?

words.en: That's fine, I'll pay the cover.

example.target: Prefiero el menú del día, gracias.
example.native: I prefer the daily set menu, thank you.

verbs.note: Stem change e to ie (except nosotros).

example.target: No, gracias, me quedo con mi pedido.
example.native: No, thank you, I'll stick with my order.

verbs.note: Quedarse con means to keep or stay with a choice.

example.target: ¿Cuánto cuesta el pescado del día?
example.native: How much is the fish of the day?

verbs.note: Stem change o to ue; mostly used as cuesta and cuestan.

example.target: Hoy le recomiendo el pescado del día.
example.native: Today I recommend the fish of the day.

verbs.note: Stem change e to ie (except nosotros).

example.target: Ana pide el menú del día.
example.native: Ana orders the daily set menu.

verbs.note: Stem change e to i (except nosotros).

passage.title: Me quedo con el menú del día
target: Ana entra a un restaurante pequeño a la hora del almuerzo y pide el menú del día.
El mesero le dice: Hoy le recomiendo el pescado del día, es muy fresco.
Ana pregunta: ¿Cuánto cuesta el pescado del día?
El mesero mira la carta y dice que el precio es 32 dólares.
Ana sonríe y responde: Gracias por la sugerencia, pero tengo un presupuesto limitado hoy.
El mesero insiste y le ofrece una guarnición extra con el pescado.
Ana dice con calma: No, gracias, me quedo con mi pedido, porque el menú del día ya incluye sopa y postre.
Al final, la cuenta es de 14 dólares y Ana deja una buena propina.
native: Ana walks into a small restaurant at lunchtime and orders the daily set menu.
The server tells her: Today I recommend the fish of the day, it is very fresh.
Ana asks: How much is the fish of the day?
The server looks at the menu and says the price is 32 dollars.
Ana smiles and answers: Thank you for the suggestion, but I have a limited budget today.
The server insists and offers her an extra side dish with the fish.
Ana says calmly: No, thank you, I'll stick with my order, because the daily set menu already includes soup and dessert.
In the end, the bill is 14 dollars and Ana leaves a good tip.

words.note: A fixed-price lunch, usually with several courses; often the best value at lunchtime.
Mexican usage; in Spain you will hear camarero.
The full menu of dishes, as opposed to the menú del día.

words.en: I prefer the daily set menu, thank you.
words.es: Prefiero el menú del día, gracias.

words.en: How much is the fish of the day?
I have a limited budget today.
No, thank you, I'll stick with my order.
words.es: No, gracias, me quedo con mi pedido.
words.note: Polite but firm; a smile and gracias keep it friendly.

words.en: If it is more expensive, I'd rather not order it.
words.es: Si es más caro, prefiero no pedirlo.

example.target: ¿Por qué cierran a las 3 de la tarde?
example.native: Why do you close at 3 in the afternoon?

verbs.note: Stem change e to ie, except in the nosotros form.

example.target: ¿Cuánto tiempo dura la comida normalmente?
example.native: How long does lunch usually last?

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb, used mostly in the third person when asking about time.

example.target: ¿A qué hora come la gente aquí?
example.native: What time do people eat here?

verbs.note: La gente takes a singular verb: la gente come, not comen.

example.target: Muchos piden café después del postre.
example.native: Many order coffee after dessert.

verbs.note: Stem change e to i, except in the nosotros form.

example.target: Si vuelvo mañana a la 1, ¿me guarda una mesa?
example.native: If I come back tomorrow at 1, will you save me a table?

verbs.note: Stem change o to ue, except in the nosotros form.

passage.title: El horario de la comida
target: Es martes y una viajera entra a un pequeño restaurante a las 3 de la tarde.
El dueño le dice: Lo siento, la cocina ya está cerrada hasta las 8.
Ella pregunta con cortesía: ¿Por qué cierran a las 3 de la tarde?
Él explica que aquí la hora de la comida es de 1 a 3 y después el personal toma un descanso.
Ella pregunta: ¿Cuánto tiempo dura la comida normalmente?
El dueño responde que un día entre semana la gente pide el menú del día y se queda casi una hora.
También dice que muchos piden café después del postre y disfrutan la sobremesa antes de pedir la cuenta.
Ella sonríe y dice: Gracias, si vuelvo mañana a la 1, ¿me guarda una mesa?
native: It is Tuesday and a traveler walks into a small restaurant at 3 in the afternoon.
The owner tells her: I'm sorry, the kitchen is already closed until 8.
She asks politely: Why do you close at 3 in the afternoon?
He explains that here lunchtime is from 1 to 3 and afterward the staff takes a break.
She asks: How long does lunch usually last?
The owner answers that on a weekday people order the daily set menu and stay almost an hour.
He also says that many order coffee after dessert and enjoy the sobremesa before asking for the check.
She smiles and says: Thanks, if I come back tomorrow at 1, will you save me a table?

words.note: In Mexico and Spain, comida usually means the main midday meal, often eaten later than lunch in the US.
Usually a fixed-price lunch with several courses.
There is no single English word for it: it means staying at the table to talk after eating.
Servers often don't bring it until you ask, because rushing you would be impolite.

words.en: What time do people eat here?
words.es: ¿A qué hora come la gente aquí?

words.en: How long does lunch usually last?
Why do you close at 3 in the afternoon?
words.es: ¿Por qué cierran a las 3 de la tarde?

words.en: Is it normal to order coffee after eating?
words.es: ¿Es normal pedir café después de comer?

words.en: Could you explain the opening hours to me, please?
words.es: ¿Me podría explicar el horario, por favor?
words.note: Podría with usted is a polite way to ask a stranger.

words.en: If I come back at 5, will it be open?

example.target: ¿Me da 200 gramos de queso, por favor?
example.native: Could you give me 200 grams of cheese, please?

verbs.note: Irregular yo form: doy.

example.target: ¿Me puede dar cubiertos y servilletas?
example.native: Could you give me utensils and napkins?

verbs.note: Stem change o to ue (except nosotros).

example.target: ¿Me rebana el jamón muy delgado, por favor?
example.native: Could you slice the ham very thin for me, please?

example.target: ¿Me lo empaca para llevar, por favor?
example.native: Could you pack it to go, please?

verbs.note: Common in Mexico and the US; in Spain people often say envolver (to wrap).

example.target: ¿Dónde se permite hacer un pícnic en el parque?
example.native: Where are picnics allowed in the park?

verbs.note: Se permite means is allowed. It is a polite way to ask about rules.

passage.title: Un pícnic desde el deli
target: Ana se acerca al mostrador de un deli cerca del parque porque quiere preparar un pícnic para 4 personas.
Ella dice: ¿Me da 300 gramos de jamón y 200 gramos de queso, por favor?
El empleado pregunta: ¿Quiere las rebanadas gruesas o delgadas?
Ana responde: Delgadas, por favor, porque son para sándwiches.
Después pregunta: ¿Me lo empaca para llevar, por favor?
El empleado pone el queso en un recipiente y todo lo demás en una bolsa.
Ana pregunta: ¿Me puede dar cubiertos y servilletas para 4 personas?
Al final pregunta: ¿Dónde se permite hacer un pícnic en el parque?
El empleado contesta: Según los letreros, el área de pícnic está junto al lago, pero confírmelo en la entrada.
native: Ana walks up to the counter of a deli near the park because she wants to put together a picnic for 4 people.
She says: Could you give me 300 grams of ham and 200 grams of cheese, please?
The clerk asks: Do you want the slices thick or thin?
Ana answers: Thin, please, because they are for sandwiches.
Then she asks: Could you pack it to go, please?
The clerk puts the cheese in a container and everything else in a bag.
Ana asks: Could you give me utensils and napkins for 4 people?
Finally she asks: Where are picnics allowed in the park?
The clerk answers: According to the signs, the picnic area is next to the lake, but check at the entrance.

words.note: Common in US Spanish; in Mexico you may also hear salchichonería, in Spain charcutería.
Deli counters in Spanish-speaking countries sell by grams or kilos; medio kilo is half a kilo.
Means the set of fork, knife and spoon.

words.en: Could you give me 300 grams of ham, please?
words.es: ¿Me da 300 gramos de jamón, por favor?
words.note: ¿Me da...? is the normal, polite way to order at a counter.

words.en: Thin, please, because they are for sandwiches.
words.es: Delgadas, por favor, porque son para sándwiches.

words.en: Could you pack it to go, please?
words.es: ¿Me lo empaca para llevar, por favor?

words.en: Could you give me utensils and napkins?
Where are picnics allowed in the park?
words.es: ¿Dónde se permite hacer un pícnic en el parque?

example.target: ¿Puede llamar al 911, por favor?
example.native: Can you call 911, please?

example.target: Mi amiga tiene una reacción alérgica.
example.native: My friend is having an allergic reaction.

verbs.note: Irregular yo form (tengo) and e to ie stem change.

example.target: Elena siente la garganta cerrada.
example.native: Elena's throat feels tight.

verbs.note: Stem change e to ie, except in the nosotros form.

example.target: ¿Puede revisar los ingredientes, por favor?
example.native: Can you check the ingredients, please?

example.target: Ella no come cacahuate porque tiene alergia.
example.native: She doesn't eat peanuts because she is allergic.

passage.title: Emergencia en el puesto
target: Estoy en un puesto de tacos cuando mi amiga Elena empieza a toser después de una mordida.
Le digo al vendedor: ¡Ayuda, por favor, mi amiga tiene una reacción alérgica!
Elena tiene alergia al cacahuate y dice que siente la garganta cerrada, así que le pregunto: ¿Necesitas tu medicamento?
Le pido a una señora: ¿Puede llamar al 911, por favor?
Luego le pregunto al vendedor: ¿La salsa tiene cacahuate?
Él revisa los ingredientes y dice: Sí, la salsa macha lleva cacahuate.
Cuando llega la ambulancia, le explico al paramédico: Ella comió un taco hace 5 minutos.
Elena ya usó el medicamento que lleva en la bolsa, y se lo digo al paramédico para que sepa qué usó y a qué hora.
native: I am at a taco stand when my friend Elena starts coughing after one bite.
I tell the vendor: Help, please, my friend is having an allergic reaction!
Elena is allergic to peanuts and says her throat feels tight, so I ask her: Do you need your medicine?
I ask a woman: Can you call 911, please?
Then I ask the vendor: Does the salsa have peanuts?
He checks the ingredients and says: Yes, the salsa macha has peanuts in it.
When the ambulance arrives, I explain to the paramedic: She ate a taco 5 minutes ago.
Elena has already used the medicine she carries in her bag, and I tell the paramedic so he knows what she used and when.

words.note: A street food stall, as in puesto de tacos.
Say tener alergia a: Tiene alergia al cacahuate.
Mexican usage; in Spain and much of South America people say maní or cacahuete.

words.en: Help, please, my friend is having an allergic reaction!
words.es: ¡Ayuda, por favor, mi amiga tiene una reacción alérgica!

words.note: 911 is the emergency number in Mexico and the US; check the local number in other countries.

words.en: She ate a taco 5 minutes ago.
words.es: Ella comió un taco hace 5 minutos.

words.en: Her medicine is in the bag.
words.es: Su medicamento está en la bolsa.

example.target: Recojo la bolsa a las 7.
example.native: I'm picking up the bag at 7.

verbs.note: Spelling change: g becomes j in the yo form (recojo) so it keeps the same sound.

example.target: Traigo mi pasaporte y el recibo.
example.native: I'm bringing my passport and the receipt.

verbs.note: Irregular yo form: traigo. The polite command to one person is traiga.

example.target: Paso a las 7 con mi pasaporte.
example.native: I'll stop by at 7 with my passport.

verbs.note: The present tense is often used for near-future plans: paso a las 7 = I'll stop by at 7.

example.target: Se la entregamos en la caja.
example.native: We'll give it to you at the register.

passage.title: La bolsa olvidada
target: Daniel llama al restaurante porque olvidó su bolsa de compras debajo de la mesa.
Él dice: Buenas tardes, almorcé ahí hoy y olvidé una bolsa debajo de la mesa.
El encargado pregunta: ¿Cómo es la bolsa y dónde estaba sentado?
Daniel explica: Es una bolsa azul de tela con asas blancas, y estaba sentado en la mesa junto a la ventana.
El encargado revisa con el mesero y confirma que la bolsa está en objetos perdidos.
Daniel pregunta: ¿A qué hora puedo pasar a recogerla?
El encargado responde: Si viene antes de las 9, se la entregamos en la caja, pero traiga una identificación.
Daniel dice: Perfecto, paso a las 7 con mi pasaporte y el recibo del almuerzo.
native: Daniel calls the restaurant because he forgot his shopping bag under the table.
He says: Good afternoon, I had lunch there today and I left a bag under the table.
The manager asks: What does the bag look like, and where were you sitting?
Daniel explains: It's a blue fabric bag with white handles, and I was sitting at the table by the window.
The manager checks with the server and confirms that the bag is in the lost and found.
Daniel asks: What time can I stop by to pick it up?
The manager answers: If you come before 9, we'll give it to you at the register, but bring some ID.
Daniel says: Perfect, I'll stop by at 7 with my passport and the lunch receipt.

words.note: Una bolsa de tela = a fabric (cloth) bag.
Handles of a bag or cup; for a door handle people say manija.
Mesero / mesera is the usual word in Mexico and the US.
The person in charge on shift; encargada for a woman.

words.en: I left a bag under the table.
words.es: Olvidé una bolsa debajo de la mesa.

words.en: I was sitting at the table by the window.
words.es: Estaba sentado en la mesa junto a la ventana.
words.note: A woman says sentada.

words.en: It's a blue fabric bag with white handles.
words.es: Es una bolsa azul de tela con asas blancas.

words.en: What time can I stop by to pick it up?
words.es: ¿A qué hora puedo pasar a recogerla?
words.note: Pasar a + infinitive = to stop by to do something.

words.en: Can you keep it for me until 7?
Do I need to bring any ID?

example.target: Pida lo que guste, yo invito.
example.native: Order whatever you like, it's my treat.

verbs.note: Yo invito means you are paying.

example.target: ¿Qué pide usted de plato fuerte?
example.native: What are you ordering for the main course?

verbs.note: Stem change (e to i), except in the nosotros form.

example.target: Le recomiendo el plato del día.
example.native: I recommend the daily special to you.

verbs.note: Stem change (e to ie), except in the nosotros form.

example.target: Pago con tarjeta, por favor.
example.native: I'm paying by card, please.

example.target: ¿Me trae la cuenta, por favor?
example.native: Could you bring me the bill, please?

verbs.note: Irregular yo form: traigo.

passage.title: Una comida de negocios
target: Invito a la señora Ruiz, mi proveedora de café, a comer en una fonda cerca del mercado.
Cuando nos sentamos, le digo: Pida lo que guste, yo invito.
Ella mira el menú del día y pregunta qué ingredientes tiene el mole.
Le pregunto al mesero, y él explica que lleva chiles, chocolate y semillas, según la receta de la casa.
Le recomiendo el plato del día como plato fuerte porque el mesero dice que es la especialidad.
Mientras comemos, le pregunto: ¿Cómo va el negocio este año?
Antes del postre, me levanto y le digo discretamente al mesero: Yo me encargo de la cuenta.
Pago con tarjeta, dejo la propina y regreso a la mesa sin decir nada.
native: I invite Mrs. Ruiz, my coffee supplier, to eat at a small restaurant near the market.
When we sit down, I tell her: Order whatever you like, it's my treat.
She looks at the lunch menu and asks what ingredients the mole has.
I ask the waiter, and he explains that it has chiles, chocolate and seeds, according to the house recipe.
I recommend the daily special as the main course because the waiter says it is the specialty.
While we eat, I ask her: How is business going this year?
Before dessert, I get up and quietly tell the waiter: I'll take care of the bill.
I pay by card, leave the tip and go back to the table without saying anything.

words.note: Use proveedora for a woman.
A set lunch menu at a fixed price, common at midday.
Mexican usage; in Spain people say camarero.
A casual, inexpensive Mexican eatery that often serves a set lunch.

words.en: Order whatever you like, it's my treat.
words.es: Pida lo que guste, yo invito.
words.note: Yo invito makes it clear that you are paying.

words.en: Would you like to try the daily special?
words.es: ¿Le gustaría probar el plato del día?

words.en: What ingredients does this dish have?
How is business going this year?
I'll take care of the bill.
words.es: Yo me encargo de la cuenta.
words.note: Say it quietly to the waiter so your guest doesn't need to offer to pay.

example.target: Pido 2 menús del día, por favor.
example.native: I'm ordering 2 daily specials, please.

verbs.note: Stem change e to i (except nosotros).

example.target: Recojo el pedido a la 1:30.
example.native: I'm picking up the order at 1:30.

verbs.note: Spelling change in yo: g becomes j (recojo).

example.target: Pago en efectivo al recogerlo.
example.native: I'll pay in cash when I pick it up.

example.target: ¿Me repite el total, por favor?
example.native: Could you repeat the total for me, please?

verbs.note: Stem change e to i (except nosotros).

passage.title: Un pedido por teléfono
target: Ana llama por teléfono a una cafetería cerca del hotel porque quiere comida para llevar.
Ella dice: Buenas tardes, quiero hacer un pedido para llevar, por favor, es para 4 personas.
Pide 2 menús del día, 2 tortas de pollo sin cebolla y 4 aguas frescas de limón.
El empleado le pregunta su nombre, y Ana contesta: Me llamo Ana Kowalski, el apellido se escribe K, O, W, A, L, S, K, I.
Luego Ana pregunta: ¿A qué hora puedo pasar a recogerlo?
El empleado dice que el total es 640 pesos y que el pedido va a estar listo a la 1:30 porque la cocina tiene muchos pedidos ahora.
Ana dice: ¿Me puede repetir el total, por favor?
El empleado confirma que son 640 pesos y que ella puede pagar en efectivo o con tarjeta al recogerlo.
native: Ana calls a café near the hotel because she wants food to go.
She says: Good afternoon, I'd like to place a takeout order, please, it's for 4 people.
She orders 2 daily specials, 2 chicken tortas without onion, and 4 lime aguas frescas.
The employee asks for her name, and Ana answers: My name is Ana Kowalski, the last name is spelled K, O, W, A, L, S, K, I.
Then Ana asks: What time can I come pick it up?
The employee says the total is 640 pesos and the order will be ready at 1:30 because the kitchen has a lot of orders right now.
Ana says: Could you repeat the total, please?
The employee confirms that it is 640 pesos and that she can pay in cash or by card when she picks it up.

words.note: Used for takeout food: comida para llevar.
In Mexico you will also hear comida corrida for a set lunch.
In Mexico a torta is a sandwich on a roll; in Spain torta can mean a cake or flatbread.

words.en: I'd like to place a takeout order, please.
words.es: Quiero hacer un pedido para llevar, por favor.

words.en: The last name is spelled K, O, W, A, L, S, K, I.
words.es: El apellido se escribe K, O, W, A, L, S, K, I.
words.note: Say each letter slowly by its Spanish name, for example K is ka and W is doble ve.

words.en: What time can I come pick it up?
words.es: ¿A qué hora puedo pasar a recogerlo?

words.en: Could you repeat the total, please?
words.es: ¿Me puede repetir el total, por favor?
words.note: Use puede (usted) with staff you don't know.

words.en: Can I pay by card when I pick it up?

example.target: Me siento aquí si no les molesta.
example.native: I'll sit here if you don't mind.

verbs.note: Stem change e to ie (except nosotros). The usted command is siéntese.

example.target: Siempre pido los tacos de ese puesto.
example.native: I always order the tacos from that stall.

verbs.note: Stem change e to i (except nosotros).

example.target: Compartimos la mesa con una pareja mayor.
example.native: We share the table with an older couple.

example.target: ¿Les molesta si pongo mi bandeja aquí?
example.native: Do you mind if I put my tray here?

verbs.note: In ¿Les molesta...? the thing that bothers is the subject, so you use the molesta form.

example.target: Si usted prueba la salsa verde, tenga cuidado porque pica mucho.
example.native: If you try the green salsa, be careful because it is very spicy.

verbs.note: Stem change o to ue (except nosotros).

passage.title: Una mesa en el mercado
target: El mercado está lleno a la hora de la comida y no hay ninguna mesa libre.
Veo una mesa compartida con una silla vacía al lado de una pareja mayor.
Me acerco con mi bandeja y pregunto: Disculpen, ¿está ocupado este asiento?
La señora sonríe y dice: No, siéntese, por favor, hay espacio para todos.
Pongo mi bolsa debajo de la silla porque no quiero ocupar su espacio.
Su plato se ve delicioso, así que les pregunto: ¿Qué pidieron?
El señor explica que son tacos de un puesto del fondo y que la salsa verde pica mucho.
Antes de irme, les digo: Muchas gracias por compartir la mesa, ¡que lo disfruten!
native: The market is full at lunchtime and there isn't a single free table.
I see a shared table with an empty chair next to an older couple.
I walk over with my tray and ask: Excuse me, is this seat taken?
The woman smiles and says: No, sit down, please, there is room for everyone.
I put my bag under the chair because I don't want to take up their space.
Their dish looks delicious, so I ask them: What did you order?
The man explains that they are tacos from a stall at the back and that the green salsa is very spicy.
Before I leave, I tell them: Thank you very much for sharing the table, enjoy your meal!

words.note: Mercado can mean an open-air market or a covered market hall.
A food stand or vendor's stall inside a market.

words.en: Excuse me, is this seat taken?
words.note: Disculpen is plural, so it speaks to the whole group at the table.

words.en: Do you mind if I sit here?
Would you recommend something from that stall?
Thank you very much for sharing the table.
words.es: Muchas gracias por compartir la mesa.

example.target: Me voy porque tengo un tren a las 3.
example.native: I'm leaving because I have a train at 3.

verbs.note: Irregular. Me voy sounds softer than just voy when you excuse yourself.

example.target: Espero el plato fuerte desde hace 40 minutos.
example.native: I've been waiting for the main course for 40 minutes.

example.target: Pago las bebidas con tarjeta.
example.native: I'm paying for the drinks by card.

example.target: ¿Me trae la cuenta, por favor?
example.native: Could you bring me the bill, please?

verbs.note: Irregular yo form: traigo.

example.target: ¿Puede cancelar el pedido, por favor?
example.native: Can you cancel the order, please?

passage.title: Una espera demasiado larga
target: Ana lleva 40 minutos en la mesa y su plato fuerte todavía no llega.
Llama al mesero con calma y le dice: Disculpe, llevo 40 minutos esperando el plato fuerte.
El mesero explica que hay un retraso en la cocina porque hoy hay mucha gente.
Ana responde amablemente: Lo siento, tengo que irme porque tengo un tren a las 3.
Luego pregunta: Si el plato no está listo, ¿puede cancelar el pedido?
También dice: ¿Me trae la cuenta de las bebidas, por favor?
El mesero trae la cuenta con 2 refrescos y Ana paga con tarjeta.
Ella deja una pequeña propina y dice: No se preocupe, no es su culpa.
native: Ana has been at the table for 40 minutes and her main course still hasn't arrived.
She calls the waiter calmly and says: Excuse me, I've been waiting 40 minutes for the main course.
The waiter explains that there is a delay in the kitchen because there are a lot of people today.
Ana replies kindly: I'm sorry, I have to go because I have a train at 3.
Then she asks: If the dish isn't ready, can you cancel the order?
She also says: Could you bring me the bill for the drinks, please?
The waiter brings the bill with 2 sodas and Ana pays by card.
She leaves a small tip and says: Don't worry, it's not your fault.

words.note: Common in Mexico; you will also hear plato principal.
Mexico and the US; in Spain people say camarero.

words.en: Excuse me, I've been waiting 40 minutes for the main course.
words.es: Disculpe, llevo 40 minutos esperando el plato fuerte.
words.note: Llevar + time + -ando/-iendo is the natural way to say how long you have been doing something.

words.en: I'm sorry, I have to go.
If the dish isn't ready, can you cancel the order?
words.es: Si el plato no está listo, ¿puede cancelar el pedido?

words.en: Could you bring me the bill for the drinks, please?
words.es: ¿Me trae la cuenta de las bebidas, por favor?

words.en: Don't worry, it's not your fault.
words.es: No se preocupe, no es su culpa.
words.note: Polite usted form; a kind way to leave without a scene.

example.target: Pido una mesa para 5 personas.
example.native: I ask for a table for 5 people.

verbs.note: Stem change e to i (except nosotros).

example.target: ¿Puede revisar los ingredientes con la cocina?
example.native: Can you check the ingredients with the kitchen?

example.target: El mesero quita el cargo de la cuenta.
example.native: The server removes the charge from the bill.

example.target: ¿El menú del día incluye postre?
example.native: Does the lunch special include dessert?

verbs.note: Adds a y in every form except nosotros.

example.target: Dividimos la cuenta entre todos.
example.native: We split the bill among everyone.

passage.title: Una comida larga con amigos
target: Llego al restaurante y pido una mesa para 5 personas y una silla para niños para mi sobrina.
Le digo al mesero: Mi amiga tiene alergia grave a los cacahuates, ¿puede revisar los ingredientes con la cocina?
El mesero confirma con la cocina que el menú del día no lleva cacahuate y nos ofrece un vino caro, pero respondo: No, gracias, solo el menú del día para todos.
Después de comer, nadie se levanta porque aquí la sobremesa es una costumbre importante, y platicamos una hora sobre el viaje, la familia y los planes para mañana.
Cuando llega la cuenta, veo un cargo por 2 postres que nadie pidió.
Le explico con calma: Creo que hay un cargo que no pedimos, ¿lo puede revisar?
El mesero quita el cargo y yo pregunto: ¿Está incluida la propina?
Al salir, le doy las gracias porque cuidó muy bien a mi amiga y a mi sobrina.
native: I arrive at the restaurant and ask for a table for 5 people and a child's chair for my niece.
I tell the server: My friend has a severe peanut allergy, can you check the ingredients with the kitchen?
The server confirms with the kitchen that the lunch special has no peanuts and offers us an expensive wine, but I answer: No, thank you, just the lunch special for everyone.
After eating, nobody gets up because here the after-meal conversation is an important custom, and we chat for an hour about the trip, family and plans for tomorrow.
When the bill arrives, I see a charge for 2 desserts that nobody ordered.
I explain calmly: I think there is a charge we didn't order, can you check it?
The server removes the charge and I ask: Is the tip included?
On the way out, I thank him because he took very good care of my friend and my niece.

words.note: In Mexico you may also hear periquera for a high chair.
Mesera for a woman. Common in Mexico and the US.
Mexican usage; in Spain and much of South America people say maní or cacahuetes.
A fixed-price lunch, often with soup, a main dish and a drink.
Staying at the table to talk after eating is normal; nobody will rush you.

words.en: My friend has a severe peanut allergy.
words.es: Mi amiga tiene alergia grave a los cacahuates.
words.note: Say grave to show it is serious, then ask them to check with the kitchen.

words.en: Does this dish have peanut or is it made near peanuts?
words.es: ¿Este plato lleva cacahuate o se prepara cerca de cacahuates?

words.en: No, thank you, just the lunch special for everyone.
words.es: No, gracias, solo el menú del día para todos.

words.en: I think there is a charge we didn't order.
words.es: Creo que hay un cargo que no pedimos.
words.note: Creo que softens the complaint and keeps it polite.

words.en: Can you split the bill for us, please?
words.es: ¿Nos puede dividir la cuenta, por favor?
